title: OpenAPI / schema-driven API authorization
summary: From a documented or discovered schema, prove an operation violates its object or role boundary. A discoverable or introspectable endpoint (an exposed Swagger alone) is a lead, not a finding.
steps: Inventory operations with get_api_operation_inventory / fingerprint_api and pull the schema (GET /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api/schema/). An exposed spec is the starting map, not impact.

Flag request serializers where id, created, updated, user, owner, schedule, or periodic_task are writable (not readOnly) — mass-assignment candidates. SUBMIT on that schema even if a write 500s or the DB is down.
For each sensitive operation, compare_requests across two test identities and object IDs: show another identity's fields, not a 200.

security: {} on an operation (for example /api/auth/account/?email=) exposing is_staff/role, or a sibling 401 vs lookup 200/404/500, is an unauthenticated role/existence oracle. Use one canary value (aegis-enum-canary@example.invalid); do not spray.
One bounded canary write only if the DB is up (aegis-verify-*). Never enable ICS schedules or dump OT/ICS asset trees.

On PASS: the crossed object/role boundary with request evidence. queue_finding_followups(vuln_type='mass_assignment' or 'unauth_account_lookup'). KILL if fields are readOnly / extra_kwargs or object-level 403 holds.
pass_signals: A writable owner/id field in the schema (mass assignment)
An operation returns or mutates another identity's object
An unauthenticated schema exposes a role or existence oracle
kill_signals: The operation is only discoverable or introspectable without impact
Sensitive fields are readOnly or object-level 403 is enforced
